name: Historic Area (Hwangnam-dong)
description: The heart of old Gyeongju, wrapped around the Daereungwon tomb mounds, Cheomseongdae observatory and Wolji Pond. Cafes, guesthouses and craft shops line calm, walkable lanes, with ancient monuments visible from almost every corner day and night.
bestFor: History lovers wanting to walk or cycle between ancient sights daily
cons: Busy with tourists in peak season

name: Bomun Lake Resort District
tagline: Lakeside resort calm on the edge
description: A landscaped resort zone east of the centre, built around scenic Bomun Lake. Hotels, spas, cherry-lined paths and lakeside cafes make it the polished, leisure-focused side of Gyeongju, quieter midweek and popular with weekend visitors and cyclists.
bestFor: Nomads wanting quiet lakeside walks, cafes and comfortable hotel-style stays
cons: A bus ride from downtown amenities

name: Downtown Seongdong
description: The practical centre near the old station and Seongdong traditional market. This is where locals shop, eat and gather, with affordable restaurants, pubs, banks and the best concentration of everyday services and evening buzz in the city.
bestFor: Budget-minded nomads wanting local food, markets and everyday convenience nearby

name: Bulguksa Temple Side
tagline: Wooded temple foothills to the east
description: The eastern edge below Toham mountain, home to the UNESCO Bulguksa temple and the Seokguram grotto. Greener and more spread out, it suits those wanting quiet, nature and heritage over city bustle, with buses linking back to the centre.
bestFor: Quiet-seeking nomads who value nature, hiking and temple heritage over city life
pros: Next to famous UNESCO temple sites
